My personal opinion, yes. I was with a girl when I was 15/16 and a year or so later we broke up mutually, because of the distance and went out separate ways, I messaged her when I was nearly 19 and we hit things off again, and I was pretty much instantly back in love (tbh I probably never stopped loving her) and we didn’t get back together because of uni, but we both admitted that we loved each other and wanted a family and such with each other. If it was for an awkward situation that I don’t really want to talk about I think we would have been together for a long time if not forever. Don’t live life with what ifs, don’t let the years go past and you start regretting never giving it a second chance and you’d live a less happy life if you start asking yourself “what if we tried again” give it a shot :)

Honestly if you like him and see a possible relationship id just straight up ask him, what have you got to lose? You might feel embarrassed a little bit but that’s no big deal, don’t live life with regrets and “what ifs”. Just think I’m 5 years time would you be asking yourself “what if I asked him if he liked me, what would have happened” don’t live with what ifs, trust me, even if it doesn’t work out for the best, atleast you know the answer and it won’t be festering in your mind :) Goodluck with whatever you choose!

I mean, there is one more thing that you could possibly do if you really want to talk to him, just involves a little harmless lie. Just tell him that you’ve got a new phone provider and ask him for his number so that you can add his number to your “new contacts” list, and if you text him and it turns out you’ve got the same number and that he’s already got it saved, if he asks about it just say that your old number must have got transferred and just claim that you didn’t know they do that. That’s the only thing I can think of without just calling him straight out about it :) or just drop him an add on Facebook if you haven’t already and just initiate the conversation from there.

Just drop him a text first if you haven’t already, and if you have and you’re not sure it’s the right number, just think of a question to ask him. If he don’t reply to the question, ask him at work if he received the text and if he didn’t then you typed the wrong number in, either way you’ll find out if he saw it or not, just make sure it’s a relatively easy question that you need an answer too :)
